english.title: Knowingly / recklessly provide false information / a document to obtain grant of an exemption licence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowing or being reckless as to whether

(A)_[information, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION..), was false in a material respect,]_
(B)_[a document, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DOCUMENT..), was not what it purported to be,]_

provided it to the Treasury for the purpose of the grant of a licence exempting you from a direction to limit or cease your business
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 31 of Schedule 7 to the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing/being reckless as to whether information was false in a material respect, OR
a document that was not what it purported to be
provided it to the Treasury for the purpose of the grant of a licence
exempting you from a direction to limit/cease your business

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The penalty for this offence has changed from indictable only to now being an either way offence, this is with effect from 1/4/17. If this offence has been committed on or after this date then use H18855 CJS Code TR08017.
(ii) Paragraph 30 of Schedule 7 to the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 provides:-
30(2) No offence is committed if the person took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to ensure that the requirement would be complied with.
30(3) In deciding whether a person has committed an offence under this paragraph the court must consider whether the person followed any relevant guidance that was at the time-
(a) issued by a supervisory authority or any other appropriate body,
(b) approved by the Treasury, and (c) published in a manner approved by the Treasury as suitable in their opinion to bring the guidance to the attention of persons likely to be affected by it.
30(4) In sub-paragraph (3) "appropriate body" means a body that regulates or is representative of any trade, profession, business or employment carried on by the alleged offender.
